analysis_notes.bechina_language_check: The source text of Torah LM2 #64 (3 sentences) contains NO instance of the word 'בְּחִינַת' or any explicit parallel-nature equation. The structure is entirely causal/genealogical: (1) wealthy leaders are literally mad — observed fact; (2) money makes one mad, because money derives from (מִנְּפִילַת) the fallen wealth of the prophets, and prophecy made the prophet appear mad; (3) in the negidim, this process produces complete madness. None of these statements is a bechina (shared essence); all are eitza (derivation and causation).
analysis_notes.dataset_gap_note: Reference 1064 is entirely absent from torahData.js. No edges of any type exist for LM2 Torah 64. This Torah has never been entered into the dataset.
analysis_notes.source_text_concepts: The Torah introduces six key concepts: (1) מָמוֹן (money/wealth) — the material substance that causes madness; (2) שִׁגָּעוֹן (madness/insanity) — the result; (3) נְגִידִים (wealthy communal leaders) — the human subjects in whom the madness appears; (4) נְבִיאִים (prophets) — the holy origin-point of the wealth pattern; (5) עֲשִׁירוּת הַנְּבִיאִים (prophetic wealth) — the original, holy form of the wealth; (6) נְפִילַת הָעֲשִׁירוּת (the fallen wealth) — the degraded form that becomes ordinary money. However, these concepts are connected by causal/genealogical relationships only, not by bechina equalities. They therefore do not form bechina-based packages.
analysis_notes.evil_mirror_note: This Torah has no classical good/evil mirror structure. It describes a single phenomenon — the madness of the wealthy — traced to its spiritual genealogy in prophecy. There is no opposing righteous domain discussed. The teaching is observational and explanatory, not prescriptive.
analysis_notes.recommendation: This Torah should be entered into the dataset with eitza-type edges. The primary causal chain is: עֲשִׁירוּת הַנְּבִיאִים → (נְפִילַת הָעֲשִׁירוּת =) מָמוֹן → שִׁגָּעוֹן. A secondary eitza edge: נְבוּאָה → הִתְנַהֲגוּת כְּמִשְׁתַּגֵּעַ (prophecy causes the prophet to appear mad). No bechina edges are warranted from this text.
